goals: Quantify precipitation partitioning (runoff, ET, recharge) across elevation and soil gradients
Validate water table depth against USGS wells
Validate snow water equivalent against SNOTEL stations
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (via NLDAS precipitation/temperature gradient and snow physics)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves the vertical partitioning processes (snow, ET, soil moisture, recharge) at each location. NLDAS-2 forcing at 0.125° provides spatially-varying precipitation/temperature that correlates with the basin's 1625 m elevation range, enabling elevation-gradient analysis. Stratified spatial sampling across elevation and soil captures the basin's heterogeneity.

answerable: Elevation/snow control on partitioning (NLDAS resolves basin-scale precip/temp gradient; ELM simulates snow)
Soil texture control on drainage and recharge
Water table depth (with WTD-informed warm start)
Recharge flux to aquifer (QDRAI, with spin-up)

not_answerable.why: ELM single-column produces no native integrated streamflow (no routing, no lateral transport). USGS gauges available but cannot be compared without routing/aggregation.
not_answerable.needs: Runoff routing and aggregation to basin outlet

not_answerable.why: No flux towers available in-domain. ET is simulated but cannot be validated co-located.
not_answerable.needs: Flux tower observations or analog-site ET dataset

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by elevation and soil texture
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 soil classes = 6 strata. Sample 2–3 columns per stratum (light replication to capture within-stratum variability) = 12–18, use 15. This resolves the elevation × soil interaction that controls partitioning.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition (800–1400 m) where partitioning sensitivity to temperature/snow is highest. Within each elevation band, place columns in contrasting topographic positions: valley bottoms (fine soils, shallow water table, high recharge potential) and hillslopes (coarse soils, deeper water table, lower recharge). Validation columns are pinned exactly to observation sites (SNOTEL stations at high elevation, USGS wells distributed across elevation).
sampling_strategy.replication: 2–3 columns per stratum to capture spatial variability within each elevation × soil combination and assess representativeness.

sampling_plan.reason: Isolate rain-dominated partitioning with rapid infiltration and minimal snow influence
Isolate rain-dominated partitioning with slower drainage and higher soil moisture retention

sampling_plan.group: mid-elevation, coarse soil (rain-snow transition, fast drainage)
sampling_plan.reason: Capture transition-zone partitioning where snowmelt timing and soil drainage interact most strongly

sampling_plan.group: mid-elevation, fine soil (rain-snow transition, slow drainage)
sampling_plan.reason: Capture transition-zone partitioning with higher soil moisture retention and delayed drainage
Isolate snow-dominated partitioning with rapid snowmelt infiltration and drainage
Isolate snow-dominated partitioning with slower snowmelt infiltration and sustained soil moisture
Co-located SWE validation at all 6 available SNOTEL stations

sampling_plan.group: USGS well validation sites (distributed across elevation)
sampling_plan.reason: Co-located water table depth validation at wells spanning low to high elevation

validation_design.comparison: co-located: ELM H2OSNO at SNOTEL coordinates vs observed peak SWE
co-located: ELM ZWT at well coordinates vs observed WTD time series
NOT FEASIBLE: ELM produces no native integrated streamflow (single-column, no routing). Validation requires routing/aggregation capability.
NOT FEASIBLE: no flux towers in-domain. Could propose analog-site process validation (literature ET values for similar forest/shrub ecosystems), but this is weak and not co-located.

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (1980-2018, full period for interannual variability), native SSURGO soil at each column location, WTD-informed warm start from Fan (2013) equilibrium WTD to initialize aquifer storage and avoid recharge spin-up artifacts

requires_capabilities.why: Recharge (QDRAI) is a target variable. Without warm start, columns cold-start at default WTD ~8.8 m and recharge reads ~0 during spin-up (initialization artifact). Warm start sets initial aquifer storage from Fan equilibrium WTD, enabling meaningful recharge quantification from the start.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Recharge quantification and water table validation

requires_capabilities.capability: Runoff routing and aggregation to basin outlet
requires_capabilities.why: USGS stream gauges are available (93 stations) but ELM single-column produces no native integrated streamflow (no lateral transport, no routing). Validation requires aggregating column runoff and routing to gauge locations.

requires_capabilities.capability: Flux tower observations or analog-site ET dataset
requires_capabilities.why: ET is a target partitioning component but no flux towers exist in-domain. Validation requires either in-domain flux towers or a curated analog-site dataset (literature values for similar ecosystems).

requires_capabilities.capability: SSURGO soil data ingest and per-column assignment
requires_capabilities.why: Soil texture is a stratification driver. Columns must be assigned SSURGO soil properties (texture, hydraulic parameters) at their coordinates.

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL station coordinate lookup and data ingest
requires_capabilities.why: SWE validation requires SNOTEL station coordinates (for column placement) and observed SWE time series (for comparison).

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well coordinate lookup and WTD data ingest
requires_capabilities.why: WTD validation requires USGS well coordinates (for column placement) and observed WTD time series (for comparison).

requires_capabilities.capability: HUC8 boundary resolver and elevation sampling
requires_capabilities.why: Stratification by elevation requires querying elevation (DEM) at candidate column locations within the HUC8 boundary to assign columns to elevation bands.

assumptions: NLDAS-2 forcing at 0.125° adequately resolves the basin-scale precipitation and temperature gradient across 1625 m of relief (sub-12 km terrain is unresolved but basin-scale gradient is captured)
SNOTEL stations are representative of high-elevation snow conditions despite 12 km forcing cells averaging over terrain (expect underestimation at ridgetop stations)
Fan (2013) equilibrium WTD provides a reasonable initial water table for ELM's 1-D aquifer (some drift expected as ELM equilibrium differs from Fan's lateral-flow equilibrium)
USGS well density is sufficient for distributed WTD validation (assumed ~5 wells span the elevation gradient; actual count depends on data query)
USGS stream gauge records are too sparse for meaningful validation without routing (brief states 'sparse daily records')
Soil texture classes (coarse vs fine) can be derived from SSURGO texture data at column coordinates
open_questions: What is the actual density and spatial distribution of USGS wells in the Naches basin (assumed ~5 for validation)?
Are SNOTEL station coordinates and observed SWE time series readily available in a queryable format?
What is the preferred forcing period for the baseline runs: full 1980-2018 (interannual variability) or a representative subset (e.g. 2000-2018, lower cost)?
Should exploratory columns include replication at identical coordinates (pure model stochasticity check) or only spatial replication (different coordinates within a stratum)?
Is there interest in a sensitivity experiment varying forcing period (wet vs dry years) to assess partitioning response to climate variability?
